the effect of the quartz is a dose-dependent one, the response to 0.2 mg of quartz being very small and that to 5 mg being very large.

the effect of quartz, when administered by intratrachel instillation, is to produce an acute inflammatory response, characterized by an increase in the number of alveolar free cells, and a decrease in the number of macrophages in lavage fluid.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellular response to quartz is biphasic and is characterized by a rapid initial response, followed by a more prolonged phase.
the response of the rat lung to quartz, as measured by the indices investigated, was a function of both time after exposure and dose.

quartz is a very effective stimulant for the alveolar macro-phages, and that the response of the macrophage population to a given dose of quartz is not constant with time, but is dependent on the dose of quartz and the time of observation after instillation.

the response of the lung is not simply a function of the amount of quartz administered but also depends on its duration of residence in the lung, the time after administration, and the time of day of the measurement.
